meta.scope: Mexico batch 9 — Judicial expansion (procuración + clearer federal/state impartición) + first CDMX / alcaldías layer. Begins the municipal zoom (CDMX first, then Guadalajara metro).

candidates.title: Censo Nacional de Procuración de Justicia Estatal (CNPJE) / National Census of State Prosecution
candidates.description: Annual census of the Fiscalías / Procuradurías Generales de Justicia of the 32 federal entities. Covers structure, resources, investigation files (carpetas de investigación), determinations, alternative dispute resolution, and forensic services. Designated Información de Interés Nacional; continuous annual series.
candidates.notes: Core prosecution-side counterpart to the impartición (courts) censuses. 2025 results covering 2024: ~2.14 million investigation files opened nationally (96.3% by state fiscalías). Estado de México, CDMX and Guanajuato account for large shares. Completes the justice-system statistical triangle with ENVIPE (victimization) and CNIJE (courts).

candidates.title: Censo Nacional de Procuración de Justicia Federal (CNPJF) / National Census of Federal Prosecution
candidates.description: Annual census of the Fiscalía General de la República (FGR). Parallel product to the state prosecution census; covers federal investigation activity, structure and resources.
candidates.notes: Federal leg of the prosecution censuses. Together with CNPJE it provides the full picture of public prosecution in Mexico. Published in coordinated CNPJF-E releases.

candidates.title: Censo Nacional de Impartición de Justicia Federal (CNIJF) / National Census of Federal Justice Administration
candidates.description: Annual census of the federal judiciary (SCJN, electoral tribunal, circuit and district courts under the CJF, agrarian tribunals). Covers structure, caseload, resources and related functions. Complements the state impartición census (CNIJE).
candidates.notes: Clarifies the federal courts node previously bundled with the state one. 2025 results include SCJN caseload (e.g. ~16 370 jurisdictional matters in 2024), amparo volumes in circuit and district courts, and overall federal + state judicial budget and staffing figures.

candidates.title: Anuario Estadístico e Indicadores de Derechos Humanos del Poder Judicial de la Ciudad de México
candidates.publisher: Poder Judicial de la Ciudad de México (PJCDMX)
candidates.description: Annual statistical yearbook of the CDMX judiciary. Tracks caseload (filings, sentences, hearings, agreements), resources, processing times and a large set of human-rights / fair-trial indicators. Continuous series (15+ editions).
candidates.notes: Strong local judicial product. 2024 edition contains 284 indicators with historical series. Also publishes higher-frequency ‘Justicia en cifras’ snapshots. Direct municipal/state-level justice node for the capital.

candidates.title: CNGMD — Demarcaciones territoriales (alcaldías) de la Ciudad de México
candidates.description: Component of the Censo Nacional de Gobiernos Municipales y Demarcaciones Territoriales focused on the 16 alcaldías of CDMX. Covers integration of the alcaldía councils, human/material/budgetary resources, and performance in government, public security, civil protection, civic justice, water/sanitation and solid waste.
candidates.notes: Primary structural source for the 16 alcaldías. Biennial. Treats alcaldías as the municipal-level unit for CDMX. Essential for any zoom into Iztapalapa, Gustavo A. Madero, Álvaro Obregón, etc.

candidates.title: Sistema de Indicadores de la Ciudad de México (SI CDMX) / IPDP indicator system
candidates.publisher: Instituto de Planeación Democrática y Prospectiva (IPDP) de la Ciudad de México
candidates.description: Public indicator platform maintained by the CDMX planning institute. Hosts development, programme and rights indicators for the city and its alcaldías, linked to the local planning system and government programmes.
candidates.notes: Local monitoring system mandated by the CDMX Constitution and Planning Law. Provides a city-level and alcaldía-level dashboard layer that re-uses and presents official statistics for policy tracking.

candidates.title: Evalúa CDMX — evaluaciones y mediciones de política social
candidates.publisher: Consejo de Evaluación del Desarrollo Social de la Ciudad de México (Evalúa CDMX)
candidates.description: Evaluation body that produces assessments and social-development measurements for CDMX programmes and conditions (including social-development indices at fine geographic scales).
candidates.notes: City-level analogue to the former CONEVAL function. Produces and uses fine-grained social indicators (e.g. Índice de Desarrollo Social at block level) that complement national multidimensional poverty statistics for the capital.

candidates.title: Alcaldía Iztapalapa — statistical and administrative profile
candidates.publisher: Alcaldía Iztapalapa / INEGI (via CNGMD, census, DENUE, etc.)
candidates.description: Largest alcaldía by population (~1.8 million in 2020). Profile assembled from national census, CNGMD, DENUE, local government reporting and city indicator systems. Serves as the first deep municipal zoom node.
referenced_by: Censo de Población y Vivienda (alcaldía tabulations)
candidates.notes: Prototype lowest-level node. Iztapalapa is the most populous demarcation. Most of its statistical identity comes from national programmes disaggregated to alcaldía level plus the CNGMD structural data. Qualifies under the expanded rule via continuous citation in city and national statistical products and in local planning documents.

candidates.title: Alcaldía Gustavo A. Madero — statistical and administrative profile
candidates.region: Ciudad de México — Gustavo A. Madero
candidates.description: Second-tier large alcaldía by population. Same data architecture as Iztapalapa (census, CNGMD, DENUE, city indicators, local administration).
candidates.notes: Second deep municipal zoom example within CDMX. Establishes the pattern for other large alcaldías if needed later.

candidates.title: Ciudad de México (entidad federativa) — core statistical identity
candidates.publisher: INEGI + Gobierno de la Ciudad de México
candidates.description: CDMX as a federal entity: population, economic activity (ITAEE / state accounts), public finances, justice (PJCDMX), government structure and the full set of national programmes disaggregated to the entity. Acts as the parent node for the 16 alcaldías.
candidates.notes: Bridge node between national series and the alcaldía layer. CDMX accounts for a large share of national GDP and has distinctive institutional arrangements (alcaldías instead of classic municipios).

proposed_edges.basis: Prosecution census supplies institutional and caseload data; ENVIPE supplies victimization and dark-figure estimates that contextualise prosecution volumes.
Federal and state impartición censuses together cover the full court system.
Local judicial yearbook operates in the same justice-statistics ecosystem as the national state impartición census; both describe court structure and caseload for CDMX.
CNGMD is the principal structural statistical source for each alcaldía.
Population and housing characteristics of the alcaldía come from the national census tabulations.
Entity-level economic activity is measured by ITAEE.
